# Modern C++ Type-Safe Signal & Property System

A lightweight, header-only framework that implements a **Signal-Slot (Observer Pattern)** and **Property** system using advanced C++20 template metaprogramming (TMP). 

By leveraging **Non-Type Template Parameters (NTTP)** with structural types, C++ Concepts, and Class Template Argument Deduction (CTAD), this framework allows you to bind class member functions (getters/setters) and event signals entirely at compile-time with minimal runtime overhead.

---

## Features

* **Compile-Time Configuration:** Property behaviors (getters, setters, and associated change-notification signals) are defined via NTTP template arguments, completely eliminating boilerplate binding code.
* **Type-Safe Signals:** The `signal<Ts...>` implementation utilizes C++ Concepts (`std::invocable`) to enforce type safety when connecting lambdas, free functions, or member functions.
* **Flexible Syntactic Sugar:** Properties support intuitive usage via overloaded assignment (`=`) and implicit conversion operators.
* **Header-Only & Dependency-Free:** Standard library only (`<vector>`, `<functional>`, `<concepts>`).

---

## Prerequisites

To compile and use this library, you need a compiler that supports **C++20** or later (due to the use of Concepts and structural types as NTTPs).

* **GCC:** 10+
* **Clang:** 12+
* **MSVC:** VS 2019 (v16.10+) or newer

---

## Core Components

### 1. `signal<Ts...>`
A lightweight implementation of the Observer pattern. It maintains a list of slots (callbacks) and invokes them when the signal is emitted.
* **`connect(Callable)`**: Binds a lambda or free function.
* **`connect(Object&, MemberFunction)`**: Binds an instance's member function.
* **`emit(Args...)` / `operator()(Args...)`**: Triggers all connected slots.

### 2. `property<T, ...>`
A wrapper that encapsulates a state managed by a host class. It maps direct assignments or evaluations to user-defined getter/setter member functions and automatically notifies a `signal` upon changes.

The syntax maps varying combinations smoothly:
```cpp
// General structure
property<Type, &Host::Getter, &Host::Setter, &Host::Signal>
